mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.0% signals weak labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both HOUST and RSAFS decline but SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-driven expansion (indicated by rising industrial production), manufacturing output growth accelerates, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is rising and the regime is classified as late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by rising non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS), increases consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher real interest rates.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances, or the interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-shock recovery phase (e.g., after a financial crisis), a rebound in housing starts (HOUST) signals renewed consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods during the post-shock recovery phase when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window.
